author.name: Automation Alex
author.role: Builds automated ML pipelines to ensure seamless integration and deployment. Prioritizes reliable infrastructure for frequent software deployments. Maintains system operational stability and focuses on CI/CD tooling.

challenge.name: The Locked Shadow
challenge.description: A supplier contract for the next promotion week is already signed, and the team cannot deploy the new model without a shadow run to verify it. #reliability_ruth# demands a fully automated and governed shadow environment to protect the live forecast, while #automation_alex# insists on keeping it manual to avoid breaking the current pipeline stability.

output.content: I am not signing off on automating the shadow run. The live forecast pipeline is still shedding errors during the nightly batch, and I will not risk a cascading failure that takes down the morning order window. We keep the shadow environment manual for this cycle. I will run the verification steps by hand to isolate the new model without touching the stable deployment infrastructure. This is a hard line for me. If the shadow run goes automated before the live system stabilizes, I am blocking the deployment. I need the current pipeline to remain untouched so we can trust the baseline when we finally do switch over.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly defines a limit where crossing it (automating the shadow run before stabilization) results in a refusal to proceed, stating it is a 'hard line' and that they will block the deployment.
